title: dedicated-autoscaler: refactor burst controls + utilization reporting (stability + observability)
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleet customers have intermittently observed burst-induced queueing and poor visibility into burst token consumption. This PR refactors the token-bucket based burst controller, tightens throughput guarantees, and expands utilization reporting to give SREs and customers clearer signals for autoscaler decisions.

What this does: refactor the burst token bucket into a single well-tested module with explicit state transitions, add a new per-fleet burst_usage metric (burst_tokens_consumed_total + burst_tokens_remaining), and emit detailed queueing histograms when bursts cause wait times > 50ms. Tighten autoscaler guarantees by adding a soft throughput reserve (configurable per-fleet) so canary and guaranteed traffic are less likely to evict each other.

Design notes: the refactor centralizes token accounting and decouples decision logic (should_grant_burst) from side-effects (emit_metrics, persist_state). This allows deterministic unit tests and easier mocking in smoke tests. The metrics follow Prometheus naming conventions. New config: dedicated.fleet.burst.soft_reserve_percent (default: "10").

Compatibility: backward compatible default behavior preserved; operators can opt-in to soft_reserve. There are no API surface changes.

Testing: unit tests cover edge cases (concurrent grants, rollover, negative consumption), integration tests added in perf-canary to validate throughput guarantees under synthetic load, manual validation against staging fleet showing reduced tail queueing. CI initially failed lint on a renamed function and one flaky test; both were addressed.

Rollout plan: feature gated behind a runtime flag (feature.dedicated.burst_refactor) and a canary rollout across two small fleets for 48h before full rollout. If regression detected revert flag.

release_notes:
- Refactor burst token-bucket controller for determinism and stability
- New metrics: dedicated_fleet_burst_tokens_consumed_total, dedicated_fleet_burst_tokens_remaining, dedicated_fleet_burst_queueing_ms_bucket
- Add soft_reserve_percent per-fleet to improve throughput guarantees under bursty load
- Observability: dashboard updated and perf canary validated reduced queueing tail latency
notes_for_ops: Default behavior unchanged. To enable new soft reserve behavior toggle feature.dedicated.burst_refactor and optionally set dedicated.fleet.burst.soft_reserve_percent (0-50). Monitor dedicated_fleet_burst_queueing_ms_bucket and burst_tokens_remaining; rollback if sustained increases in request throttling observed.
